article.title: How to Install a Towel Bar That Won't Pull Out
article.summary: Install a bathroom towel bar that stays put: choose the height, find studs or use the right anchors, mount the brackets level, and set the bar.
article.body:
Most towel bars fail because the anchors in the box can't handle a wet towel being yanked every day. Mounting into a stud or using stronger anchors fixes that. This guide covers drywall, with notes for tile.

Affiliate disclosure: some links in this guide are affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. We only recommend products we'd use ourselves.

Safety: check for pipes and wires before drilling, especially near sinks, showers and switches. Wear safety glasses.

Steps

  1. Pick the height and spot

    A common height is about 48 in from the floor to the bar, or about 42 in for a hand towel. Center the bar over the space it serves, and make sure a towel won't hang onto a light switch or block a door.

    Done right: you've marked a center point and a height, and a towel held there doesn't block anything.

  2. Find a stud for at least one bracket

    Scan with a stud finder. If one bracket can land on a stud, adjust the bar position slightly so it does; a screw into a stud is the strongest mount. Most bars are long enough that both brackets rarely hit studs.

    Done right: you know which bracket goes into a stud and which needs an anchor.

  3. Mark level bracket holes

    Use the paper template if one is included, or measure the bar's bracket spacing. Draw a level line and mark both brackets on it.

    Done right: both bracket marks sit on the same level line.

  4. Drill and anchor

    Into a stud, drill a small pilot hole and drive the screw directly. Into hollow drywall, skip the small plastic anchors in the box and use heavy-duty drywall anchors such as snap toggles or self-drilling metal anchors, drilled to the size on the package. On tile, put tape over the spot and drill with a carbide or diamond tile bit at slow speed.

    Done right: each anchor sits flush and spins only when the screw is driven, not on its own.

  5. Mount the brackets and bar

    Screw the mounting plates to the wall. Slide the bar into the posts, push the posts over the plates, and tighten the set screws underneath with the hex key.

    Done right: the bar is level and doesn't move when you pull down firmly with both hands.

Hire a handyman if: you need to drill through glass tile, stone or a fiberglass shower surround, or the drywall around an old towel bar is crumbling and needs patching first.

FAQ

How high should a towel bar be?

About 48 in from the floor for a bath towel and about 42 in for a hand towel are common heights.

What anchor is best for a towel bar?

A stud is best. In hollow drywall, snap toggles or heavy-duty self-drilling anchors hold far better than the small plastic anchors that come with most bars.

How do I fix a towel bar that pulled out of the wall?

Patch or move past the damaged hole, then remount with a toggle anchor, which grips the back of the drywall over a wider area.

Can you install a towel bar on tile?

Yes. Tape the tile, drill slowly with a carbide or diamond bit, and use anchors that suit the wall behind the tile.
